tools.name: google_connect
tools.title: Connect a Google account
tools.description: Returns the Google consent link that connects one Google account to the caller in a hal workspace (Gmail and Drive). The user opens it in a browser, chooses the account and accepts; the link is valid ten minutes, once. Calling it on a workspace already connected replaces that account after the new consent.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

tools.name: google_disconnect
tools.title: Disconnect a Google account
tools.description: Revokes at Google the account the caller connected to a hal workspace, then deletes its stored token. Refused by name when the workspace has no connected account.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

tools.name: drive_search
tools.title: Search Drive
tools.description: Files whose name contains `query`, optionally only the children of `parent_id` and only of `mime_type`; trashed files never. The Drive query is built here from these parameters and returned as `q`. Every file carries md5Checksum, size, mimeType, parents, driveId and webViewLink (md5Checksum and size are absent on a Google-native file).

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

query.description: A fragment of the file name

parent_id.description: Only the direct children of this folder

mime_type.description: Only this MIME type, e.g. application/pdf or application/vnd.google-apps.folder

tools.name: drive_get
tools.title: Get a Drive file
tools.description: One file's metadata — md5Checksum, size, mimeType, parents, driveId, webViewLink — and whether this account may move it (capabilities.canMoveItemWithinDrive, canMoveItemOutOfDrive). No md5Checksum and no size: a Google-native file.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

file_id.description: A Drive file or folder id

tools.name: drive_resolve_path
tools.title: Resolve a folder path
tools.description: The folder ids along `path` (folder names, as get_filing_path returns them), from the workspace's storage.root (whoami → storage). Names match with case, accents and surrounding blanks ignored; two matching folders are refused with both. Without create_missing, missing folders are returned in `missing` and nothing is created: show them to the user, and after their yes call again with create_missing=true.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

path.description: Folder names from the top-level folder down

create_missing.description: Create the missing folders — only after the user said yes

tools.name: drive_find_duplicate
tools.title: Find a duplicate in a folder
tools.description: Before filing a file into `folder_id`: `identical` (a file there has this md5 — write nothing, link the record), `same_name_other_content` (a file there has this name but other bytes — stop and ask), or `none`. Without md5 (a Google-native file) only the name, and the size when given, can be compared, and the answer says so.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

folder_id.description: A Drive file or folder id

name.description: The name the file will have in the folder

tools.name: drive_move
tools.title: Move a Drive file
tools.description: Moves a file (never a folder) into `to_folder_id`, renamed to `new_name` when given, in one call: it is never in two places. Refused by name when Google does not let this account move it, when the file or the folder lies outside the drive of the workspace's storage.root, and when the folder already holds the same bytes or the same name (drive_find_duplicate's verdict). Returns the file with its webViewLink and md5Checksum.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

file_id.description: A Drive file id — a folder is refused

to_folder_id.description: A Drive file or folder id

tools.name: drive_rename
tools.title: Rename a Drive file
tools.description: Renames a file or folder in place.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

file_id.description: A Drive file or folder id

tools.name: drive_create_folder
tools.title: Create a Drive folder
tools.description: Creates the folder `name` in `parent_id`, after searching the parent again: a folder already matching it (case, accents and blanks ignored) is refused with its id.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

parent_id.description: A Drive file or folder id

tools.name: drive_trash
tools.title: Trash a duplicate
tools.description: Puts `file_id` in Drive's trash (recoverable 30 days) — only when `same_as_file_id` is another file with byte-identical content (same md5Checksum). Refused by name otherwise, and for a Google-native file, which has no md5.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

file_id.description: A Drive file or folder id

tools.name: search_emails
tools.title: Search Gmail
tools.description: Messages matching a Gmail search query, newest first: id, threadId, subject, from, date, snippet.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

query.description: Gmail search syntax, e.g. 'from:qonto has:attachment newer_than:30d'

tools.name: read_email
tools.title: Read an e-mail
tools.description: One message: headers, labels, the plain-text body (the HTML one when the message has no plain text, as body_mime_type says), and its attachments with attachmentId, filename, mimeType and size — the bytes stay at Gmail (get_attachment, drive_upload_from_gmail).

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

tools.name: draft_email
tools.title: Draft an e-mail
tools.description: Creates a Gmail draft — nothing is sent. With reply_to_message_id it sits in that message's thread. A header value holding a line break is refused.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

to.description: Recipient address(es), as a To header

reply_to_message_id.description: The Gmail message id this draft answers

content.description: The file as standard base64, no line breaks

attachments.description: At most 25 MB of base64 in all (~18.5 MB of bytes); share a larger file as a Drive link in the body

tools.name: list_labels
tools.title: List Gmail labels
tools.description: Every Gmail label, system and user: id, name, type.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.title: Get an attachment
tools.description: An attachment's bytes as standard base64, with its size and md5 (computed here — the md5Checksum drive_find_duplicate compares). To file an attachment in Drive, call drive_upload_from_gmail instead: the bytes then never pass through the conversation.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

attachment_id.description: An attachment's attachmentId, as read_email lists it

tools.name: drive_upload_from_gmail
tools.title: File a Gmail attachment in Drive
tools.description: Copies an attachment from Gmail into the Drive folder `folder_id` under `name`, server-side: the bytes never reach the caller. drive_find_duplicate runs first on the attachment's md5, name and size, and the upload is refused by name on `identical` (link the record to the file there) and on `same_name_other_content` (stop and ask). Returns the md5 and the new file with its webViewLink and md5Checksum.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

attachment_id.description: An attachment's attachmentId, as read_email lists it

name.description: The file's name in Drive (get_filing_path gives it)

tools.name: forward
tools.title: Forward an e-mail
tools.description: SENDS the message to `to` at once — there is no draft and no undo. Before calling it, show the user the recipient, the subject and every attachment (read_email) and wait for their explicit go. The forward carries `note`, the « Forwarded message » block (From, Date, Subject, To, Cc), the original body and every original attachment byte for byte, and sits in the original's thread. A header value holding a line break is refused.

workspace_slug.description: The hal workspace, as `whoami` lists it

to.description: Recipient address(es), as a To header

note.description: Text written above the forwarded message
